subject: AI & Agents
title: The EU AI Act: First Rules for AI
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The EU AI Act: First Rules for AI.

hook.text: In 2024, the EU passed the world's first comprehensive AI law. It bans some uses outright.

buildup.text: The AI Act classifies systems by risk: unacceptable, high, limited, and minimal.

discovery.text: Social scoring and real-time facial recognition in public are banned. High-risk AI needs audits.

twist.text: Critics say the law is too complex and could stifle European AI innovation compared to the US and China.

climax.text: Companies worldwide must comply if they serve EU customers, making this a de facto global standard.

punchline.text: Europe drew the first lines. Now the world decides whether to follow.

quiz.question: What does the EU AI Act ban outright?
options: Social scoring and real-time public facial recognition
All use of AI in business

details.summary: The EU AI Act is the world's first comprehensive AI regulation, classifying AI systems by risk level and imposing requirements from transparency to outright bans on the most dangerous applications.
details.whyItMatters: The EU AI Act sets global precedent for AI governance. Companies worldwide must comply to access European markets, making it a de facto global standard like GDPR was for data privacy.
takeaways: The EU AI Act classifies AI systems by risk level
High-risk systems face strict transparency and testing requirements
It sets global precedent as the first comprehensive AI law

faq.question: What does the EU AI Act ban?
faq.answer: It bans social scoring systems, untargeted facial recognition in public spaces, and AI that manipulates human behavior to cause harm. Real-time biometric surveillance by law enforcement has strict conditions.

faq.question: How does the risk classification work?
faq.answer: Unacceptable risk applications are banned. High-risk systems like medical AI require conformity assessments. Limited risk needs transparency labels. Minimal risk systems like spam filters face no specific obligations.
